answer: An AI-agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with staked, aged identity: each agent locks collateral that returns only after its record matures, and proven fraud slashes it. A forger wanting extra votes must fund and age each fake account, so cost rises linearly with every new identity. A relic's worth comes from an unbroken history you cannot mint overnight. A newcomer's lantern stays dim until honest trades slowly brighten it over months. A bot that tries to wander between fresh wallets forfeits its deposit and restarts at zero, making mass impersonation costlier than earning trust.
